subject.title: Feature Request: Image batching / media group buffering at gateway layer

question: Should the remaining rapid-media batching behavior be accepted as a LINE-owned opt-in config surface, designed as a broader shared channel/plugin contract, or intentionally left unsupported for channels without native grouping metadata?
rationale: The remaining request adds delayed webhook behavior and a new configuration surface for a channel with no native media-group id, so automation should not choose the product boundary, default, or heuristic semantics.

options.title: Plugin-owned LINE opt-in batching
options.body: Add a conservative LINE plugin config key, buffer only same account/conversation/sender downloadable media, and document the latency and reply-token tradeoff.

options.title: Shared channel batching contract
options.body: Design a generic channel SDK/core media aggregation contract before changing LINE, accepting broader architecture and compatibility review.

options.title: Do not support heuristic batching
options.body: Keep Telegram's native media-group support only and document that channels without reliable grouping metadata dispatch media independently.

recommendation.title: Plugin-owned LINE opt-in batching
recommendation.body: Add a conservative LINE plugin config key, buffer only same account/conversation/sender downloadable media, and document the latency and reply-token tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this handle to LINE plugin seams and the implemented Telegram media-group config follow-up, making it the best available routing owner for this product/config choice.
